modern: When the life of grace first begins in the soul, we do draw near to God, but with great fear and trembling. The soul, aware of its guilt and humbled by it, is overawed by the solemnity of its position; it is thrown to the ground by a sense of the greatness of Jehovah, in whose presence it stands. With unpretended shyness it takes the lowest place.

But later in life, as the Christian grows in grace, though he will never forget the solemnity of his position, and will never lose the holy awe that must surround a man of grace when he is in the presence of the God who can create or destroy, his fear has all its terror taken out of it. It becomes a holy reverence, no longer an overshadowing dread. He is called up higher, to closer access to God in Christ Jesus. Then the man of God, walking among the splendors of God, and veiling his face like the glorious cherubim with those twin wings, the blood and righteousness of Jesus Christ, will approach the throne, reverent and bowed in spirit; and seeing there a God of love, goodness and mercy, he will be more aware of God’s covenant character than of his absolute Godhead. He will see in God his goodness more than his greatness, and more of his love than of his majesty. Then the soul, bowing as humbly as before, will enjoy a more sacred freedom in prayer; for while it lies face down before the glory of the infinite God, it will be held up by the refreshing awareness of being in the presence of boundless mercy and infinite love, and by the realization of being accepted “in the Beloved.” So the believer is told to come up higher, and is enabled to use the privilege of rejoicing in God and drawing near to him in holy confidence, saying, “Abba, Father.”

modern: Yes, Lord, you don’t give up your throne when the sun goes down, nor do you leave the world all through these long winter nights to be the prey of evil. Your eyes watch us like the stars, and your arms surround us as the zodiac circles the sky. The dews of kindly sleep and all the influences of the moon are in your hand, and the alarms and solemn hours of night are equally with you. This is very sweet to me when I’m watching through the midnight hours, or tossing to and fro in anguish. There are precious fruits put out by the moon as well as by the sun: may my Lord make me a favored sharer in them.

The night of affliction is as much under the arrangement and control of the Lord of love as the bright summer days when everything is bliss. Jesus is in the storm. His love wraps the night around itself like a cloak, but to the eye of faith that black robe is hardly a disguise. From the first watch of the night until daybreak, the eternal Watcher keeps his eye on his saints, and rules over the shadows and dews of midnight for his people’s highest good. We don’t believe in rival gods of good and evil fighting for the upper hand; we hear the voice of Jehovah saying, “I create light and I create darkness; I, the Lord, do all these things.”

Gloomy times of religious indifference and social sin aren’t exempt from God’s purpose. When the altars of truth are defiled and the ways of God forsaken, the Lord’s servants weep with bitter sorrow; but they mustn’t despair, for the darkest ages are ruled by the Lord, and will come to an end at his command. What may seem defeat to us may be victory to him.

modern: The Lord Jesus Christ was eternally *rich*, glorious and exalted; but “though *he was rich*, yet for your sakes he became poor.” A rich saint can’t have true fellowship with his poor brothers and sisters unless he helps meet their needs out of what he has; in the same way (the same rule holding between the Head and the members), our divine Lord couldn’t possibly have had fellowship with us unless he had shared his own overflowing wealth with us and become poor to make us rich. If he had stayed on his throne of glory, and we had remained in the ruins of the fall without receiving his salvation, fellowship would have been impossible on both sides. Our position after the fall, apart from the covenant of grace, made it as impossible for fallen man to have fellowship with God as it is for Belial to be in harmony with Christ. So, in order that fellowship might be brought about, the rich kinsman had to give his estate to his poor relatives; the righteous Savior had to give his sinning brothers some of his own perfection; and we, the poor and guilty, had to receive from his fullness grace for grace. In this way, by giving and receiving, the One could come down from the heights and the other rise from the depths, and so they could embrace each other in true and heartfelt fellowship. Poverty must be made rich by him in whom are infinite treasures before it can dare to have fellowship; and guilt must lose itself in imputed and imparted righteousness before the soul can walk in fellowship with purity. Jesus must clothe his people in his own garments, or he can’t admit them into his palace of glory; and he must wash them in his own blood, or they will be too defiled for the embrace of his fellowship.
O believer, here is love! For *your sake* the Lord Jesus “became poor,” so that he might lift you up into fellowship with himself.

modern: We look forward to the happy day when the whole world will be converted to Christ; when the gods of the heathen will be thrown to the moles and the bats; when Roman Catholicism will be exploded, and the crescent of Mohammed will wane, never again to cast its deadly rays on the nations; when kings will bow down before the Prince of Peace and all nations will call their Redeemer blessed. Some despair of this. They see the world as a ship breaking up and going to pieces, never to float again. We know that the world and everything in it is one day to be burned up, and afterward we look for new heavens and a new earth; but we can’t read our Bibles without being convinced that:

We aren’t discouraged by the length of his delays; we aren’t disheartened by the long period he gives the church to struggle with little success and much defeat. We believe that God will never let this world, which has once seen Christ’s blood shed on it, be the devil’s stronghold forever. Christ came here to rescue this world from the hated rule of the powers of darkness. What a shout that will be when men and angels join to cry, “Hallelujah, hallelujah, for the Lord God Omnipotent reigneth!” What satisfaction it will be on that day to have had a share in the fight, to have helped break the arrows of the bow, and to have helped win the victory for our Lord! Happy are those who trust themselves to this conquering Lord and fight side by side with him, doing their little bit in his name and by his strength! How unhappy are those on the side of evil! It is a losing side, and in this matter to lose is to lose and be lost forever. Whose side are you on?

modern: Today let’s go down to Bethlehem, and in the company of the wondering shepherds and the worshiping wise men, let’s see him who was born King of the Jews; for by faith we can claim a share in him and can sing, “*Unto us* a child is born, *unto us* a son is given.” Jesus is Jehovah made flesh, our Lord and our God, and yet our brother and friend; let’s adore him and marvel at him. Let’s notice at the very first glance *his miraculous conception*. It was a thing unheard of before and unmatched since, that a virgin should conceive and bear a son. The first promise ran like this: “*The seed of the woman*,” not the offspring of the man. Since daring woman led the way in the sin that brought about Paradise lost, she, and she alone, ushers in the One who regains Paradise. Our Savior, though truly man, was in his human nature the Holy One of God. Let’s bow reverently before the holy Child whose innocence restores to humanity its ancient glory, and let’s pray that he may be formed in us, the hope of glory. Don’t fail to notice *his humble parentage*. His mother is described simply as “a virgin”: not a princess, or a prophetess, or a lady of great estate. True, the blood of kings ran in her veins; nor was her mind weak or untaught, for she could sing a song of praise most sweetly. But how humble her position was, how poor the man she was engaged to, and how miserable the lodging given to the newborn King!

*Immanuel*: God with us in our nature, in our sorrow, in our life’s work, in our punishment, in our grave; and now with us, or rather we with him, in resurrection, ascension, triumph and the splendor of his second coming.

modern: What the patriarch did early in the morning after the family festivities, the believer would do well to do for himself before he rests tonight. Amid the cheerfulness of family gatherings it is easy to slide into sinful frivolity and forget our professed character as Christians. It shouldn’t be so, but so it is: our days of feasting are very seldom days of holy enjoyment, and too often sink into unholy merriment. There is a way of rejoicing as pure and sanctifying as if one bathed in the rivers of Eden: holy gratitude should be every bit as purifying as grief. Alas for our poor hearts, that the facts prove the house of mourning better than the house of feasting! Come, believer, how have you sinned today? Have you forgotten your high calling? Have you been like others in idle words and loose talk? Then confess the sin, and flee to the sacrifice. The sacrifice sanctifies. The precious blood of the slain Lamb removes the guilt and cleans away the defilement of our sins of ignorance and carelessness. This is the best way to end Christmas Day: to wash afresh in the cleansing fountain. Believer, come to this sacrifice continually; if it is so good tonight, it is good every night. To live at the altar is the privilege of the royal priesthood. For them sin, great as it is, is still no cause for despair, since they draw near again to the sin-atoning victim, and their conscience is cleansed from dead works.

modern:
Jesus is the covenant head of his chosen. Just as every heir of flesh and blood has a personal stake in Adam, because he is the covenant head and representative of the human race under the law of works, so under the law of grace every redeemed soul is one with the Lord from heaven, since he is the Second Adam, the Sponsor and Substitute of the chosen in the new covenant of love. The apostle Paul says that Levi was in the loins of Abraham when Melchizedek met him; it is just as certain that the believer was in the loins of Jesus Christ the Mediator when, in the eternity before time, the arrangements of the covenant of grace were decreed, ratified and made sure forever. So whatever Christ has done, he has done for the whole body of his church. We were crucified in him and buried with him (read [[Col.2.10|Col. 2:10-13]]), and, to make it more wonderful still, we are risen with him and have even ascended with him to the seats on high ([[Eph.2.6|Eph. 2:6]]). This is how the church has fulfilled the law and is “accepted *in the beloved*.” This is how she is looked on with delight by the just Jehovah, for he sees her in Jesus and doesn’t look at her as separate from her covenant Head. As the anointed Redeemer of Israel, Christ Jesus has nothing apart from his church; all he has, he holds for her.

Adam’s righteousness was ours as long as he kept it, and his sin was ours the moment he committed it; and in the same way, all that the Second Adam is or does is ours as well as his, since he is our representative. Here is the foundation of the covenant of grace. This gracious system of representation and substitution, which moved Justin Martyr to cry out, “O blessed change, O sweet permutation!” is the very groundwork of the gospel of our salvation, and is to be received with strong faith and rapturous joy.

modern:
The Lord Jesus is in the middle of his church; he walks among the golden lampstands; his promise is, “Lo, I am with you alway.” He is as surely with us now as he was with the disciples by the lake when they saw a fire of coals with fish laid on it, and bread. Not in the flesh, but still in real truth, Jesus is with us. And it is a blessed truth, for where Jesus is, *love catches fire*. Of all the things in the world that can set the heart burning, there’s nothing like the presence of Jesus! A glimpse of him so overwhelms us that we are ready to say, “Turn away thine eyes from me, for they have overcome me.” Even the scent of the aloes and myrrh and cassia that drips from his perfumed garments makes the sick and the faint grow strong. Let there be just a moment’s leaning of the head on that gracious breast, and a receiving of his divine love into our poor cold hearts, and we are cold no longer, but glow like seraphs, equal to every task and able to bear every suffering. If we know that Jesus is with us, *every power will be developed* and every grace strengthened, and we will throw ourselves into the Lord’s service with heart and soul and strength. So the presence of Christ is to be desired above all things.

*His presence will be felt most by those who are most like him*. If you want to see Christ, you must grow to be like him. Bring yourself, by the power of the Spirit, into union with Christ’s desires and motives and plans of action, and you are likely to be favored with his company. Remember, *his presence may be had*. His promise is as true as ever. He delights to be with us. If he doesn’t come, it’s because we hinder him by our indifference. He will reveal himself to our earnest prayers, and will graciously let himself be held by our pleadings and our tears, for these are the golden chains that bind Jesus to his people.
